nodes.title: The weight-two Shimura isomorphism is Hecke-equivariant
nodes.statement: For N ≥ 5, the Hodge decomposition gives S₂(Γ₁(N), ℂ) ⊕ S̄₂(Γ₁(N), ℂ) ≅ H¹(X₁(N)^an, ℤ) ⊗ ℂ, and it identifies ⟨n⟩ ⊕ ⟨n⟩̄ with ⟨n⟩^*, T_p ⊕ T̄_p with T_p^* = (π₁^{(p)})_* ∘ (π₂^{(p)})^* and w_N ⊕ w̄_N with w^*_{e^{2πi/N}}, where π₁^{(p)}, π₂^{(p)} : X₁(N, p) → X₁(N) are the degeneracy maps and (π₁^{(p)})_* is the trace.
hypotheses: N ≥ 5 (for N < 5 both sides vanish); the Betti-side integral structure is Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 8's modular-symbol lattice, whose comparison with H¹(X₁(N)^an, ℤ) is part of this stage.
proofSteps: Hodge decomposition of the compact Riemann surface X₁(N)^an with H⁰(Ω¹) = S₂(Γ₁(N), ℂ).
Compute T_p^* on H¹ through the trace along π₁^{(p)} (stalkwise sum with ramification multiplicities) and pullback along π₂^{(p)}; compare with the double-coset action on cusp forms.
Diamond operators and w_ζ are induced by automorphisms, so pullback commutes with the Hodge decomposition.
acceptance: Conrad omits the proof of the compatibility; a complete proof must check the trace formula against the classical double coset (ModularCurvesPartII R12.5 normalises the differentials and Hecke operators).

hypotheses: The cup-product pairing is perfect; the Petersson integral converges by exponential decay at the cusps.
proofSteps: Use the normalization of Sh in Conrad §5.1, pp. 63–65, rather than unscaled f dz. Compute the wedge of the resulting harmonic representatives and evaluate using the specified i-orientation; with the non-normalized Petersson measure the factor is 4π as in Theorem 5.2, p. 66.

w^*_{ζ^j} ∘ w^*_ζ = ⟨j⟩^*, a unit commuting with T₁(N), reduces general ζ to e^{2πi/N}.

nodes.statement: For the universal elliptic curve f:E→Y₁(N), N≥5, construct L_B=R¹f_an,*ℤ and L_{ℓ,n}=R¹f_et,*ℤ/ℓⁿ, with ℓ invertible on the base. Their geometric fibres are H¹ of the elliptic fibre, locally free of rank two. For r=k−2≥0 set L_r=Sym^r L, of rank r+1. The coefficient maps along an isogeny are induced by its pullback on relative H¹; integral lattices and duals are retained before any inversion of ℓ.

nodes.statement: For a smooth open complex or étale curve with finite puncture set D, the support-forgetting map fits into the cohomology sequence of j_!L→Rj_*L→i_*i^*Rj_*L. In degree one, H¹_par is ker(H¹(Y,L)→⊕_{c∈D}H¹(I_c,L_c)); the neighboring H⁰ and H²_c terms are retained. For trivial A coefficients on a connected curve with s cusps, 0→H¹(X,A)→H¹(Y,A)→A^D→A→0 is exact, where the last map sums residues (and the étale terms carry the residue Tate twist).
hypotheses: ℓ is invertible for étale coefficients; local punctured-disc/tame inertia comparison is part of the supplier request.

proofSteps: Apply the localization triangle for j_! and Rj_*; compute each boundary stalk by local inertia cohomology.
For constant coefficients the local invariant and residue groups are rank one; global orientation/trace identifies the final sum map.
Pullbacks and traces of finite correspondences induce morphisms of this sequence.

nodes.title: Integral comparison and change of level
nodes.statement: For the supplied smooth finite-type modular curves over Q̄, a chosen embedding Q̄↪C, and finite locally constant ℤ/ℓⁿ coefficients from the universal family, Artin comparison gives H^i_et(Y,L_{r,ℓ,n})≅H^i_B(Y_an,L_{r,B}/ℓⁿ), with compact-support analogues and their support maps. These identify finite parabolic images. After proving the required inverse-limit exactness and finite generation, they give the adic comparison; for r=0 this also identifies the actual compact-curve lattice with Mathlib’s pro-étale EllAdicCohomology in degree one. Pullback, trace, cup product and level maps commute with comparison.

Derived-limit obstructions must be eliminated by finite coefficient Mittag–Leffler systems; reduction modulo π commutes only under the torsion hypotheses of localized-freeness.
proofSteps: Import the general étale–Betti comparison required by RS-06.
Use naturality with j_!→Rj_* and finite correspondences; apply the coefficient comparison from relative-coefficient-system.
Apply finite generation and Mittag–Leffler exactness to the finite systems; separately request the comparison with Mathlib’s pro-étale carrier.

nodes.title: Parabolic Poincaré pairing
nodes.statement: The elliptic cup product L⊗L→A(−1) induces Sym^r L⊗Sym^r L→A(−r). For A=K it is perfect. For finite or integral coefficients assume r! is a unit (in particular ℓ>r); then the symmetrized tensor pairing is perfect with the chosen normalization. On parabolic H¹ it induces a pairing into A(−r−1), alternating for even r and symmetric for odd r. The rational pairing is nondegenerate; integral/finite perfection is exported only in the localized setting of localized-freeness, where boundary and coefficient-reduction obstructions vanish. Pullback and trace are adjoint.
hypotheses: A complete DVR O of residue characteristic ℓ; finite coefficients O/πⁿ; integral conclusion additionally needs finite freeness and boundary conditions.
At ℓ≤r no integral perfectness is inferred from Deligne’s rational statement; a different divided-power lattice would require its own comparison.
proofSteps: Form the coefficient pairing by symmetrizing products of the alternating rank-two elliptic pairing; invert r! when necessary.
Apply EDC.2 curve duality to j_*L and its dual, or Betti Poincaré–Lefschetz duality.
Restrict the compact-support/ordinary pairing to their common image, using the vanishing and exactness hypotheses to prove integral perfection.
The sign is the coefficient sign (−1)^r times the degree-one cup sign.
acceptance: r=0 gives an alternating curve pairing; r=1 gives a symmetric pairing.
A rationally perfect pairing whose determinant is divisible by ℓ is not an integral acceptance case.

nodes.title: Non-Eisenstein removal of the boundary
nodes.statement: For weight-two constant coefficients at a torsion-free congruence level and an anemic Hecke maximal ideal m of residue characteristic ℓ≥3, call m non-Eisenstein if its good-prime eigenvalues are not ψ₁(q)+qψ₂(q) with ψ₁,ψ₂ finite congruence characters and diamond product ψ₁ψ₂. The cusp boundary modules and H⁰(Y,O/π) have only those Eisenstein eigensystems. Thus they vanish after localization at m, and H¹_c→H¹ identifies its localized image with ordinary localized H¹. For Sym^r coefficients the same implication is a separate requested calculation, not an assertion from the weight-two source.
hypotheses: Anemic operators exclude level and residue-characteristic primes; fine level removes stabilizer torsion.
In weight two this definition is an algebraic Hecke condition; the identification with residual Galois irreducibility is a consequence in R19, not a prerequisite here.
proofSteps: Compute the two parts of the good-prime correspondence on cusps from R14.1: one permutes with multiplicity q and the other with multiplicity one.
Diagonalize the finite cusp action after extending residue coefficients; obtain the displayed sums of congruence characters.
Apply exact localization to the boundary sequence; compute H⁰ by constants.
acceptance: An Eisenstein maximal ideal may retain cusp classes.
The statement does not demand a Galois representation theorem to define non-Eisenstein localization.

nodes.title: Finite generation and localized integral freeness
nodes.statement: For a torsion-free congruence modular curve Y and a finite free O-local system L, H¹(Y,L) is O-finite. If H⁰(Y,L/π)_m=0, the localized group H¹(Y,L)_m is O-torsion-free, hence O-free; if in addition the boundary sequence localizes to zero, it equals H¹_par(Y,L)_m, and reduction gives H¹_par(Y,L)_m/πⁿ≅H¹_par(Y,L/πⁿ)_m. Constant weight-two coefficients satisfy these conditions at the non-Eisenstein ideals of boundary-non-eisenstein. Higher-weight claims retain the displayed vanishing conditions until the separate boundary gap is resolved.
hypotheses: O is a complete DVR finite over ℤ_ℓ; anemic localization is a direct summand of the completed O-finite Hecke module.
Use a finite graph deformation retract of the noncompact torsion-free quotient; its two-term cochain complex has finite free terms.
proofSteps: Import the Fuchsian finite-type/free-group model and twisted cochains.
The coefficient sequence 0→L→L→L/π→0 shows π-torsion in H¹ is the image of H⁰(L/π); the localized vanishing kills it.
A finite torsion-free module over a DVR is free; graph cohomological dimension one removes H² obstructions to reduction.
Use the boundary sequence at O and finite levels to identify ordinary and parabolic groups under the stated vanishings.
acceptance: No freeness over the integral Hecke algebra is asserted.
At level divisible by ℓ, or with coarse stabilizers, the displayed geometric and vanishing hypotheses must be checked afresh.

The integral statement refines the rational parabolic realization with explicit torsion hypotheses.

nodes.title: Modular symbols and the geometric lattice
nodes.statement: For the supplied torsion-free congruence quotient, identify the homological modular-symbol module of ModularForms Layer 8 with relative H₁(X_an,D;Sym^r lattice) using its Manin presentation, with the appropriate coefficient dual when pairing against L_r. The boundary map corresponds to restriction to cusp divisors. The cuspidal kernel modulo torsion pairs with H¹_par; rationally, and integrally under the torsion and perfectness hypotheses already displayed, this gives its dual cohomological lattice. The period map of ModularForms is integration against this homology and acts on symbols by transpose, not by an identification of forms with symbols.

Integral conclusions use the local coefficient dual and saturation; the whole symbol module contains boundary and may contain torsion.
proofSteps: Import Manin generators and relations and the relative singular-chain model.
Send a cusp difference with coefficient to its geodesic chain; use polygon relations and endpoint boundary maps to obtain the comparison.
Use duality to pass from cuspidal relative homology to parabolic cohomology, keeping the torsion-free quotient and coefficient dual explicit.
Match integration and Hecke pull-push to the existing period functional.

The boundary quotient is not erroneously retained as part of compact H¹.

nodes.title: Compact weight-two Ihara and saturation
nodes.statement: For N≥5 and prime p∤N, let X′ be the compact curve of Γ₁(N)∩Γ₀(p). The map δ₁^*+δ_p^*:H¹(X₁(N),F_ℓ)²→H¹(X′,F_ℓ) is injective for every prime ℓ.
